doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: New York, Birdland and the Major Bowes contest
summary: Gibbs says New York accepted him royally; he was house bandleader at Birdland six months a year and on the road the rest. He won Major Bowes at thirteen and jokes about hotel cockroaches.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I’m a hero. I grew up in New York and it’s very fortunate, I really did well in New York. I was accepted royally. I was the house band leader at Birdland in my younger days. There would always be Count Basie, Sarah Vaughan, Terry Gibbs, Duke Ellington, Dinah Washington, Terry Gibbs. But I was there six months a year, and I’d be on the road the other six months. But I was always accepted and it was great. I got a chance to play with everybody in the world.
Was it here where you won the Major Bowes contest?

Yeah. I grew up in Brooklyn. And I was a Major Bowes. But I was thirteen, in fact, last December was 64 years that I’d been on the road. I know every cockroach in every hotel in the world. I’ve been on the road — you name it — the cockroaches became my friends. There’s a few in this hotel.
